commenti.body: Why do some tv series focus so much on side characters and side quests? It’s super distracting. Lessons in Chemistry and Julia. They’re distracting in a jarring manner. Feel like an ordeal. The minute the story gets good, now it goes to a side quest for another character. First season of The Morning Show is perfect. Every character is integral to the plot, and their story. Lessons in Chemistry, like, get to the cooking show already! The side quest of the neighbor lady needs to be a different show. And I’d watch it before I’d watch Brie doing an offensive impression of a person on the spectrum. Sex and the City made sense because it was all about relationships and sex. There was an overarching theme. The Queen’s Gambit stayed focused.
Pandering in order to attract the largest sets of viewers with multiple storylines. One is bound to keep you engaged
What ended up being yall’s favorite films from this year?

I thought ”Poor Things” was a big disappointment. Emma Stone has a showy role, but brought no soul to it. She’s going on this journey of discovery that needs sensitivity and joy, it needs a passion for life, and instead she kind of plays the character as emotionally deadened. I don’t get it. The movie felt pretty pointless because of it.

Either Angela Schanelec's Music or Radu Jude's Do Not Expect Too Much From The End of The World. I see some people counting De Humani Corporis Fabrica as a 2023 film and if we'd allow it, it'd go on my list as well.

Music is a stunning exercise in patience, pauses and ellipses, all in the vein of Straub and Huilliet. Radu Jude's newest is an excellent satire critique of corporate and capitalist hypocrisy done in seriously funny satire. Then there's De Humani Corporis Fabrica, which makes Brakhage's The Act of Seeing look tame in comparison, all with a sound perspective on the French inpatient system and the clinicians within them (especially radical in its final sequence). It's a funny counterpart to Cronenberg's Crimes of the Future and the 'surgery is sex' polemic.
PLSSS rec some good ass films. Like your go-to movies that leave you with a message or a feeling but aren't soul-crushingly boring. Ill tell u what I think of them once i finish them.

I'd have to say Poor Things just a bit more so than Holdovers. 

Still a bunch to catch up on. 

How about you?
Oppenheimer, but I haven’t seen much this year. I need to get caught up
